evidence.quoted_text: for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(overrides)) child[name] = value;
evidence.reason: buildChildEnv copies allowlisted names verbatim, including an inherited PATH, then writes overrides under the caller's exact key. On Windows environment names are case-insensitive, and Node's spawn uses the first lexicographic case variant, so an override keyed `Path` can leave the inherited `PATH` as the effective value. That contradicts the documented “overrides ALWAYS win” behavior. Normalizing Windows names before applying overrides is an ordinary correctness fix; POSIX must remain case-sensitive.
